native_result.query: What kind of demographic disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated?
native_result.HypoA: Gender disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated, with males having higher median wealth than females.
native_result.HypoB: Among individuals jailed between 1985 and 1994 (ever_jailed=1, n=289), 1985 median wealth shows demographic disparities along race and sex: white respondents held the highest median wealth ($2,200, n=69) versus black ($320, n=159) and hispanic ($0, n=61); the same ordering holds in the more reliable male subgroups (white male $2,000 > black male $800 ≈ hispanic male $700). The racial gap is driven mainly by differing shares of zero/negative wealth (white 31.9% vs black 47.8% vs hispanic 52.5%) rather than by wealth levels among those with positive wealth (medians converge to $4,400–$6,000 after excluding wealth ≤ 0). Female respondents (n=37) had median wealth of $0 with 70.3% at or below zero versus males ($1,000 median, 41.3% ≤ 0), but female cross-cells are very small (n=9–16), so sex-based contrasts are preliminary observations only. Overall, the ever-jailed group's 1985 median wealth ($720) was about one-fifth of the never-jailed group's ($3,600). Qualifications: 'hipanic' is treated as hispanic; ever_jailed refers to incarceration during 1985–1994, so its relation to 1985 wealth is temporally ambiguous and all statements are descriptive associations, not causal claims.
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded data/nls_incarceration_processed.csv (12,013 rows, no missing values). Verified distributions of race/sex/ever_jailed. Main sample: ever_jailed=1 (n=289). Primary metric: median composite_wealth_1985 with Q1/Q3/IQR and n by race, sex, and race×sex cross-cells; negative values retained (net-wealth interpretation). Background reference: full-sample median 3,400 (IQR 16,000) and ever_jailed=0 median 3,600. Sensitivity: medians after excluding wealth ≤ 0, mean-vs-median comparison, share of wealth ≤ 0 by group. Small female cells (n≤16) flagged as low-certainty preliminary observations; conclusions anchored on male subgroups and single-variable groupings. Summation convention of the composite could not be verified internally (no component columns); noted as a limitation.

Malformed judge output raises an evaluation error; no hidden retries.
evaluator_config.aggregation: recall_context * mean_accuracy_score; unmatched predicted contexts stay in denominator
evaluator_config.native_behavior_preserved: Variable/relation comparisons receive full hypotheses for each matched context pair.

details.score_scope: Reference agreement of submitted hypothesis; execution is not independently verified by this native metric.
